links.outcome: Trade-off between accuracy and readability of LLM-transformed reports across reading grade levels
links.effect: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors; higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability. Preferences peaked at grade 16 and declined at grade 17, particularly among laypersons.
links.quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

links.outcome: Stakeholder preference and readability across reading grade levels 7-17 of LLM-transformed reports
links.effect: Higher grade levels (12-17) generally preferred due to better accuracy; further increasing grade levels reduced readability sharply, limiting preference.
links.quote: Higher-grade levels were generally preferred due to better accuracy, with a range of 12-17.
